headline: Inclusion is active welcome—making space for people to belong and contribute as they are
universal_truth: Diversity is presence; inclusion is participation; you can be present without belonging
fun_facts: Employees who feel included are 3x more likely to be engaged at work
Inclusion isn't passive tolerance—it requires active effort to welcome and integrate
The opposite of exclusion isn't just presence—it's genuine belonging
discussion_questions: When have you felt included versus just tolerated?
How do you actively include others?
What barriers to inclusion exist in your environments?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You can be in a room without being part of the conversation. You can be on a team without being welcomed. Inclusion isn't just presence—it's belonging. Making room means actively creating space where everyone can contribute.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Diversity gets people in the room. But what makes them actually feel welcome? What's the difference between presence and inclusion?

options.text: Inclusion requires active welcome—not just allowing presence but creating belonging; it means inviting contribution, valuing difference, and removing barriers to participation
options.response: Yes. Inclusion is a verb—it takes action. Diverse people can be present and still excluded through culture, assumption, and inaction. Active inclusion creates actual belonging.

options.text: Inclusion means treating everyone the same
options.response: Treating people the same can actually exclude—different people need different things to belong...

q1.title: Passive vs Active
q1.script: Passive inclusion says 'you're allowed to be here.' Active inclusion says 'we want you here and value what you bring.' The difference determines whether presence becomes belonging.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Passive vs Active"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Barrier Removal
q2.script: Inclusion requires removing barriers—not just opening doors but clearing paths. What prevents participation? What makes contribution difficult? Identifying and removing barriers creates inclusion.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Your Role
q3.script: You can create inclusion wherever you are. Welcome the newcomer. Invite the quiet person to speak. Notice who's missing from conversations. Inclusion is practiced by individuals, not just organizations.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Diversity is presence; inclusion is participation. You can be present without belonging. Actively make room for everyone.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 327. Tomorrow, we'll explore feeling what others feel—empathy. Until then, notice who might need more active inclusion.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Inclusion Practice - Who Needs Welcome?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify and act on inclusion opportunities
growTrack.activity: In your environments—work, social, community—who is present but not included? What barriers prevent their participation? What's one action you could take to create more belonging for someone?
